---
title: "Explore a 1D convolution"
toc: false
page-layout: full
---

A convolution applies the same short filter at every location in a signal. This
explorer uses a simple sensor trace: select a filter, move its five-sample
window, and watch the corresponding response signal grow one local dot product
at a time.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What to watch

The upper plot overlays the original sensor trace with the selected five-point
kernel. The kernel slides with the active window. At every sample time, its
weights multiply the five values under the window, and their sum becomes one
point in the lower response trace.
:::

```{=html}
<div id="convolution-explorer" class="convolution-explorer" aria-label="Interactive one-dimensional convolution explorer">
  <div class="convolution-control-panel">
    <div class="convolution-kernel-copy">
      <span class="convolution-eyebrow">Choose a five-tap kernel</span>
      <p id="convolution-kernel-description">A change detector compares the samples immediately after and before the center.</p>
    </div>
    <div id="convolution-kernel-controls" class="convolution-kernel-controls" role="group" aria-label="Choose a convolution kernel">
      <button type="button" class="convolution-kernel-card" data-kernel="average">
        <span class="convolution-kernel-label">Smooth</span>
        <svg class="convolution-kernel-thumbnail" data-kernel-thumbnail="average" aria-hidden="true"></svg>
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="convolution-kernel-card is-active" data-kernel="change" aria-pressed="true">
        <span class="convolution-kernel-label">Changes</span>
        <svg class="convolution-kernel-thumbnail" data-kernel-thumbnail="change" aria-hidden="true"></svg>
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="convolution-kernel-card" data-kernel="peak">
        <span class="convolution-kernel-label">Peaks / dips</span>
        <svg class="convolution-kernel-thumbnail" data-kernel-thumbnail="peak" aria-hidden="true"></svg>
      </button>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="convolution-toolbar clt-buttons">
    <button id="convolution-previous" type="button">Previous window</button>
    <button id="convolution-next" type="button" class="regression-sampling-primary">Next window</button>
    <button id="convolution-play" type="button">Play all</button>
    <button id="convolution-reset" type="button">Reset</button>
    <output id="convolution-status" class="convolution-status" aria-live="polite"></output>
  </div>

  <div class="convolution-workbench">
    <section class="convolution-panel convolution-visual-panel" aria-labelledby="convolution-visual-heading">
      <div class="convolution-panel-heading">
        <h2 id="convolution-visual-heading">Input with a moving kernel</h2>
        <p>The shaded window identifies the five values being multiplied. The kernel curve slides over the input trace; the response grows from left to right below it.</p>
      </div>
      <figure class="convolution-figure">
        <svg id="convolution-main-chart" role="img" aria-label="Original sensor trace overlaid with a moving five-point kernel and a convolution response"></svg>
      </figure>
      <p id="convolution-response-insight" class="convolution-response-insight"></p>
    </section>

    <section class="convolution-panel convolution-calculation-panel" aria-labelledby="convolution-calculation-heading">
      <div class="convolution-panel-heading">
        <h2 id="convolution-calculation-heading">One local weighted sum</h2>
        <p>Each filter value is reused at every valid sample time.</p>
      </div>
      <div id="convolution-calculation" class="convolution-calculation" aria-live="polite"></div>
    </section>
  </div>
</div>
```

The output is shown only where the full five-sample window lies inside the
measured trace. In a CNN, the filter values are learned from training data
rather than chosen by hand—but the local calculation is the same.
